title: Telling a story: yesterday, tomorrow, the weekend
goal: Turn events into a story — linking words, time order, and how Malaysians talk about their weekend.
bekal: putting time words in a natural place
talking about the weekend with Malaysian leisure vocabulary

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Monday morning in the cafeteria
dialogs.intro: Monday morning. Aina hasn't even sat down before asking where Sarah disappeared to all weekend.

lines.speaker: Aina:
lines.text: Eh, hujung minggu semalam awak ke mana? Bilik kosong je.
lines.id: Hey, where did you go last weekend? Your room was empty the whole time.
lines.literal: eh, end week yesterday you to where? room empty just.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Saya pergi Bukit Bintang dengan kawan dari Indonesia.
lines.id: I went to Bukit Bintang with a friend from Indonesia.
lines.literal: I go Bukit Bintang with friend from Indonesia.

lines.speaker: Aina:
lines.text: Best tak? Buat apa kat sana?
lines.id: Was it fun? What did you do there?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Mula-mula kami makan tengah hari kat Jalan Alor.

lines.text: Lepas tu kami jalan-jalan kat Pavilion. Sejuk sangat dalam tu.

lines.id: What time did you get back?

notes: **Hujung minggu** = weekend (literally "end of the week"). *Hujung* = end, tip, and it appears in many phrases: *hujung tahun* (end of the year), *hujung bulan* (end of the month), *hujung jalan* (end of the road).

**Best** is an English word that has become fully Malay, and it means **fun, great, enjoyable** — not "the best". *Best tak?* = "Was it fun?", *Best gila!* = "So much fun!". All ages use it and it doesn't feel foreign at all. The native Malay equivalent is *seronok* (remember unit 3).
**Berbaloi** = worth it. A very common word: *tak berbaloi* = not worth it, *berbaloi ke?* = is it worth it?
**Air pancut** = fountain (literally "spurting water"). You'll also hear *pancutan air*.
**Sempat** = to have (enough) time to do something. **Tak sempat** = didn't have time, didn't manage to. It's used constantly: *Saya tak sempat makan* = I didn't get a chance to eat.

grammars.title: Story linking words
body: Malay storytelling uses the same word order as English: event, then linking word, then the next event. What makes it sound Malaysian is the **choice of linking words**.
after: **Lepas tu** is the most common linker in spoken Malaysian stories — you'll hear it three or four times in one short story. Copying it is the easiest way to make your stories sound natural.
⚠️ **Walhal** means **when in fact, whereas** — it points out a contradiction: *Dia cakap dah siap, walhal belum mula lagi.* (He said he'd finished, when in fact he hasn't even started.)

blocks.text: Time words can go at the start or the end of a sentence. In spoken Malaysian stories they tend to go **at the start**:

head: Malay
English
rows: Last week we went to Melaka.
Last year I didn't know him yet.

blocks.text: ⚠️ Note **pagi tadi** and **malam tadi** — *tadi* (earlier) comes **after** the part of the day: "morning earlier" = this morning, "night earlier" = last night. (Indonesian puts it first: *tadi pagi*.) For the future it's the other way round: **nanti petang**, **nanti malam** — *nanti* (later) comes first.

head: Malay
English
Note
rows: the day after tomorrow / in three days

blocks.text: Leisure words you'll need as soon as someone invites you out:

head: Malay
English
rows: take a leisurely stroll or drive

blocks.text: **Melepak** is Malaysian slang for **hanging out** — getting together with no particular purpose, usually at a mamak stall. *Jom melepak* = "let's hang out". Young people use it all the time.

Note the word family of **sukan** = sport: *bersukan* (to do sport), *acara sukan* (sports event), *Sukan Malaysia* (the Malaysia Games). And **melancong / pelancong / pelancongan** = to travel / tourist / tourism.

blocks.title: Asking and talking about the weekend
items: **Hujung minggu ni buat apa?** — What are you doing this weekend?
**Ada plan tak?** — Got any plans?
**Jom keluar.** — Let's go out.
**Best tak?** — Was it fun?
**Berbaloi ke?** — Was it worth it?
**Penat tapi puas.** — Tired but happy.
**Lain kali kita pergi sekali.** — Next time let's go together.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the right linking word.
items: ____ kami makan, kemudian kami jalan-jalan. (at first)
Saya mandi. ____ saya keluar. (after that)
Hujan turun. ____ kami balik awal. (that's why)
____ makan, jangan lupa cuci tangan. (before)
____ kelas habis, kita jumpa kat kafe. (after)
Dia cakap dah siap, ____ belum mula lagi. (when in fact)

exercises.prompt: Translate into Malay — watch where the time word goes.
items: This morning I woke up late.
Last night it rained heavily.
Yesterday I went to KL.
Last week we went to Melaka.
He arrived the day before yesterday.
Where did you go last weekend?
First we had lunch, then we wandered around.
Was it fun?
No time, the tickets were sold out.
We finally got back at twelve midnight.
Tired but worth it.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: tu / kami / lepas / jalan-jalan
pukul / balik / kami / dua belas / akhirnya
Alor / kami / kat / makan / Jalan / mula-mula
tak / naik / menara / sempat / kami
sekali / depan / kita / minggu / pergi

answers: Mula-mula — Lepas tu — Sebab tu — Sebelum — Selepas — walhal
Pagi tadi saya bangun lambat. — Malam tadi hujan lebat. — Semalam saya pergi KL. — Minggu lepas kami ke Melaka. — Kelmarin dia sampai.

Hujung minggu semalam awak ke mana? — Mula-mula kami makan tengah hari, lepas tu jalan-jalan. — Best tak? — Tak sempat, tiket dah habis. — Akhirnya kami sampai pukul dua belas malam. — Penat tapi berbaloi.
Lepas tu kami jalan-jalan. — Akhirnya kami balik pukul dua belas. — Mula-mula kami makan kat Jalan Alor. — Kami tak sempat naik menara. — Minggu depan kita pergi sekali.
